topic.title: The waiting list
topic.claim: In India a product becomes premium the day it gets a waiting list; a queue is the only review we still trust.
topic.moment: Two new cafés on one street: the empty one stays empty, the one with a line gets a longer line.

turn.believed: we wait for things because they're good
turn.actually: we decide they're good because people are waiting

topic.because: in a market of fake reviews and forever sales, a queue feels like proof nobody could buy, and brands use scarcity on purpose
topic.payoff: We don't really want the thing. We want to have waited for it.

cover.headline: In India, a product becomes [premium] the day it gets a waiting list.
cover.sub: We don't trust what we can have today.

paragraphs: In India, a product becomes premium the day it gets a waiting list.
slides.why_swipe: it states the take; the reader wants to see it play out

paragraphs: Watch what happens outside two new cafés on the same street.
The empty one with good coffee stays empty. The one with a forty-minute line has a longer line by evening.
slides.why_swipe: the café is familiar; does it go beyond cafés?

paragraphs: Same with cars. A six-month waiting period doesn't put buyers off. It becomes the first thing they tell you.
"Booked it in March, delivery in September." Said like a medal.
slides.why_swipe: cars too; why does waiting make it better?

paragraphs: **A queue is the only review most of us still trust.**
In a market full of fake reviews, paid posts and forever sales, a line of strangers feels like real proof.
slides.why_swipe: the motive is out; do brands know this?

paragraphs: Brands have figured this out. Limited stock at launch. A booking amount. An invite-only app.
The wait isn't always a problem they're trying to solve. Sometimes it is the product.
slides.why_swipe: the dark pattern is out; how does it end for us?

paragraphs: The strange part is how well it works on us. The day something gets easy to buy, we start to doubt it.
**We don't really want the thing. We want to have waited for it.**

end.save: For the next time you're stuck in a line for coffee.
end.send: Send it to the friend who booked a car because of the waiting period.

draft.caption: What's the longest you've waited for something, just because everyone else was waiting?
draft.alt_text: A text carousel arguing that in India a waiting list makes a product feel premium, because a queue is the one review people still trust, and brands use that.
